### Summary

Structured message attachments accepted several equivalent source fields, but sandbox validation stopped after the first populated field. Telegram later processed every populated source, allowing an out-of-sandbox host path to be hidden behind an allowed attachment source.

### Impact

A sandboxed model could cause Telegram delivery to read and send a known host file that OpenClaw's sandbox media policy would reject on its own. Exploitation required a useful host path and an allowed Telegram delivery target. The issue bypassed path validation; it did not provide general filesystem listing.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade `openclaw` to `2026.8.1` or later. Until upgraded, deny Telegram attachment actions to sandboxed or lower-trust agents and reject structured attachments containing more than one source field before delivery.
summary: Structured attachments could hide unvalidated host paths
